title: Cartesian-fibration base change preserves pushouts of infinity-categories
statement:
Use the infinity-category and universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Inner fibration has the inner-horn lifting meaning of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. In this statement a Cartesian fibration $p:X\to Y$ means an inner fibration admitting a lift $x'\to x$ of every arrow $y'\to p(x)$ with specified target, such that for every $z\in X$ the square $\operatorname{Map}_X(z,x')\to\operatorname{Map}_X(z,x)$ over $\operatorname{Map}_Y(pz,y')\to\operatorname{Map}_Y(pz,px)$ is a homotopy pullback. Let $A,B,C,D$ be infinity-categories and let
$$\begin{matrix}A&\longrightarrow&B\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ C&\longrightarrow&D\end{matrix}$$
be a coherent pushout square in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. Let $p:E\to D$ be a Cartesian fibration. Then its base-change square
$$\begin{matrix}A\times_D E&\longrightarrow&B\times_D E\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ C\times_D E&\longrightarrow&E\end{matrix}$$
is a pushout in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$, with all pullbacks taken in infinity-categories. All displayed categories and the finite diagrams are taken in one sufficiently large fixed universe; no fibration condition on the arrows of the original square is imposed.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.3 and Corollary 3.3.1.4, together with the Joyal-model homotopy-pushout interpretation of a pushout in Cat_infinity (Section 4.2.4). This is the model-independent base-change consequence used in Gepner–Haugseng Proposition 5.3.16, first proof paragraph; its citation of HTT Corollary 2.4.4.5 alone omits the arbitrary-simplicial-set comparison. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical theorem.

proof.text: First compare the two conventions for Cartesian edges. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to $p^{\mathrm{op}}:E^{\mathrm{op}}\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$: order reversal exchanges $\Lambda_0^n$ with $\Lambda_n^n$ and the edge $\{0,1\}$ with $\{n-1,n\}$. On mapping spaces the arrow model of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] gives $U_{E^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,z)=U_E(z,x)^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversal of barycentric coordinates gives $|K^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|K|$: the opposite of an operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ is $i\mapsto n-\alpha(m-i)$, so the quotient identifications of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] agree under reversal. This comparison is natural in $K$. Reversing a triangle exchanges its edges $01,12$ and retains its long edge $02$; the triangle formula for composition in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] therefore identifies opposite precomposition with the postcomposition square in the statement. The natural pinch equivalences then identify the two mapping-space tests, including their homotopies. Hence the assumed lifts are precisely final-horn Cartesian lifts. For any base map $T\to D$, an inner-horn or Cartesian final-horn problem for $T\times_D E\to T$ projects to a problem for $p$; pair its filler with the prescribed simplex in $T$. Given an edge $t'\to t$ and an object $(t,e)$, choose a Cartesian lift $e'\to e$ of its image in $D$ and pair it with $t'\to t$. The preceding final-horn argument makes this pair Cartesian. Thus every degreewise base change remains a Cartesian fibration, even for a nonfibrant base.

source.place: Section 2.4.1, Cartesian/coCartesian duality; mapping-space characterization, expressed by the cited DAG criterion.

proof.text: Let $q:N(\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathrm J})\to\mathcal L$ be coherent localization at categorical equivalences. The Joyal model structure exists by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. The Quillen equivalence $\mathfrak C\dashv N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ and its identification with $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], with the derived-adjunction construction of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], identify $\mathcal L$ with $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. A quasicategory represents itself under this identification. We will use [lem-coef-cocomplete-cofibration-localization] for this model. Its hypotheses follow directly from the Joyal weak factorization systems: all objects are cofibrant because $\varnothing\to K$ is degreewise injective; factorization is given; pushouts and coproducts of cofibrations or trivial cofibrations have the same lifting property against the corresponding right class, since a compatible family of lifting problems is solved on each summand, or on the added pushout piece. All small limits and colimits of simplicial sets are formed degreewise in sets; their simplicial operators are induced by the universal property. Monomorphisms contain isomorphisms and are composition closed. Categorical equivalences contain isomorphisms directly from their functor-category test, and are composition closed by two-out-of-three; they have the stated retract closure. Thus the initial object, factorization, coproduct and cofibration-pushout hypotheses are all satisfied. In particular $q$ carries every strict pushout along a simplicial monomorphism to a coherent pushout in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. No combinatoriality or simplicial-model assertion about the Joyal structure is needed for this application.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.5.1; Section 4.2.4; agent application of the all-cofibrant cofibration-localization theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-diagram-model-rectification] to the finite ordinary square category $[1]\times[1]$ and the Joyal model. It supplies a strictly commuting square of simplicial sets whose image under $q$ is coherently equivalent to the given square, including the entire cocone. Functorial fibrant replacement, applied at all four vertices and arrows, makes its vertices quasicategories without changing its coherent equivalence class. Denote this square by $A_0\to B_0$, $A_0\to C_0$, $B_0,C_0\to D_0$. Its apex is accompanied by an equivalence $d:D_0\to D$ and compatibility homotopies for the square; equivalences of coherent diagrams are pointwise by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Form $E_0=D_0\times_D E$ degreewise; step 1 shows $p_0:E_0\to D_0$ is Cartesian. Apply [lem-coef-degreewise-cartesian-pullback-cat-infinity] to compare each degreewise Cartesian pullback, with its canonical projections, with the pullback in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$; this applies to arbitrary simplicial $K\to S$ and is natural over $S$. Applied with $S=D$, $Z=E$, $K=D_0$, this shows that $E_0$ with its projections is the infinity-categorical pullback $D_0\times_D E$; here $d$ is a categorical equivalence by (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations], being an equivalence of quasicategories. Thus it suffices to prove the result for this strict square and $p_0$: the given coherent equivalence of squares and $d$ identify their pulled-back diagrams, with all maps, by the universal property of pullback.

source.place: Section 4.2.4, strict/coherent diagram comparison; Corollary 3.3.1.4 for the pullback along d.

proof.text: Factor $A_0\to B_0$ as a monomorphism $A_0\hookrightarrow B_1$ followed by a Joyal trivial fibration $B_1\to B_0$, and do the same for $A_0\to C_0$ with middle object $C_1$. Give the middle objects their maps to $D_0$ by composition; the square therefore still commutes strictly over $D_0$. These factorizations are provided by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. The span $B_1\leftarrow A_0\to C_1$ is equivalent after $q$ to the preceding span, since both comparison maps are weak equivalences. Put $P=B_1\amalg_{A_0}C_1$ in simplicial sets. By step 2 and [lem-coef-cocomplete-cofibration-localization], $qP$ with this cocone is a pushout. The induced map $u:P\to D_0$ has image an equivalence: both its source cocone and its target cocone are pushouts of this same span. The contractibility of initial objects in the cocone category, supplied by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applies to this specified comparison. Finally $u$ is a categorical equivalence by [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences]. The ordinary-localization hypothesis is supplied by [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category], applied to $C=\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathrm J}$, $W$ the categorical equivalences and the coherent localization $q$ of step 2. Enlarge the universe so that this ordinary category is small. That node identifies $hq:C\to h\mathcal L$ with the ordinary localization, including natural transformations, so the detection theorem applies to the specified image of $u$. We have not assumed that $B_1,C_1$ or $P$ is a quasicategory.

source.place: Section 4.2.4, homotopy pushout represented by cofibrant span; comparison with its colimiting cocone.

proof.text:
For $K=A_0,B_1,C_1,P$, write $K_E=K\times_{D_0}E_0$ degreewise. There is a canonical isomorphism of simplicial sets over $E_0$,
$$(B_1)_E\amalg_{(A_0)_E}(C_1)_E\ \cong\ P_E.$$
Here is its inverse degree by degree. An $n$-simplex on the right is a pair $([t],e)$ with $[t]$ a class in $(B_1)_n\amalg_{(A_0)_n}(C_1)_n$ and the images of $t,e$ equal in $(D_0)_n$. Choose a representative $t$ in either summand and send the pair to the class of $(t,e)$. A generating relation identifying the two images of $a\in(A_0)_n$ identifies exactly the two images of $(a,e)$; its image in $D_0$ is unchanged. Thus the result is independent of the representative. It is inverse to the displayed comparison and commutes with every simplicial operator. The two pulled-back legs are monomorphisms: equality of pairs implies equality of their first coordinates, and the original legs are injective. This is a set-theoretic calculation; it imposes no fibrancy requirement on any of these four simplicial sets.

source.place: Agent degreewise pushout/pullback calculation in simplicial sets; the ordinary calculation used with Proposition 3.3.1.3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocomplete-cofibration-localization] to the monomorphism pushout of step 5. It follows that $qP_E$ is the pushout of $q(B_1)_E\leftarrow q(A_0)_E\to q(C_1)_E$. We now identify its apex. The family of relative marked model structures of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] supplies every structural hypothesis in [lem-coef-cartesian-base-equivalence-invariance]: monomorphism cofibrations, Cartesian weak equivalences, the stated fibrant objects and fiberwise criterion, sharp simplicial enrichment and tensor, and the base-change Quillen adjunctions. The tensor convention also follows explicitly from its sharp mapping formula: a map $U\times K^\sharp\to V$ over the base is exactly a compatible family of maps $U\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp\to V$, one for each simplex $\Delta^n\to K$. This is the tensor adjunction, so the tensor is $U\times K^\sharp$ as required. Apply part (1) of that node to the Cartesian fibration $p_0:E_0\to D_0$ and the categorical equivalence $u:P\to D_0$ from step 4. It gives that $P_E\to E_0$ is a categorical equivalence. In particular this invocation allows $P$ to be an arbitrary simplicial set. Replacing the pushout apex by $E_0$ using this equivalence shows that the cocone with maps induced from $B_1,C_1\to D_0$ is a pushout in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.1.3, with the relative marked model structure establishing its hypotheses.

proof.text: It remains to compare this cocone with the one in the question. For every small simplicial set $K\to D_0$, [lem-coef-degreewise-cartesian-pullback-cat-infinity], applied to the Cartesian fibration $p_0:E_0\to D_0$ of quasicategories, shows that $q(K_E)$ computes $qK\times_{qD_0}qE_0$, with its canonical projections. No quasicategory hypothesis on $K$ is needed for this. Apply this to $A_0,B_1,C_1$. The equivalences $qB_1\simeq B_0$ and $qC_1\simeq C_0$ over $D_0$ from step 4 identify the three vertices and arrows of the span in step 6 with the intrinsic pullback span for $A_0,B_0,C_0$. Thus this intrinsic pullback cocone with apex $E_0$ is a pushout. Finally apply the coherent equivalence of squares and the pullback comparison of step 3 to identify it with the displayed cocone $A\times_D E\to B\times_D E$, $A\times_D E\to C\times_D E$, with apex $E$. A coherent equivalence of cocones preserves the property of being initial in the cocone category, or equivalently its mapping-space universal property, by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. This proves the required pushout with exactly its specified maps. All replacements, finite shapes and degreewise constructions stay in the fixed universe, and the localization may be taken in the larger universe stipulated in the statement.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.1.4; Section 4.2.4; invariance of the colimiting cocone under coherent equivalence.
